p.x:
Thailand has three main seasons. The hot season is from March to May. The temperature is often over 35 degrees, and the sky is usually clear and sunny. Many people go to the beach or visit an island in the south.
The rainy season is from June to October. It is cloudy on many days, and there is often a big storm in the afternoon. The rain is good for farmers, because rice needs a lot of water. But the streets in Bangkok can get very wet!
The cool season is from November to February. This is the best time for tourists. In the north, it can be quite cold at night, especially in the mountains, and some people travel there to see the forest and the fog in the morning. But don't expect snow. It never snows in Thailand!

Last April, Bangkok had been suffering from a heatwave for two weeks. Every day the scorching sun pushed the temperature to 40 degrees, and the air was so humid that even sitting still made you sweat. So when the weather forecast said that a big storm was coming, many people were relieved.
At around nine in the evening, the wind suddenly became stronger. Then the lightning started, lighting up the whole sky, followed by thunder so loud that car alarms went off. The rain was heavy for two hours, and in some parts of the city the streets flooded within minutes. Motorbike riders had to push their bikes through water up to their knees.
The next morning, the air felt fresh and almost cool, though nobody would call it freezing. Some trees had fallen, and there was rubbish everywhere, but the city landscape looked green and clean again. "I hate floods," said one shopkeeper, "but after two weeks of that heat, I'm not complaining."

For centuries, Thai farmers could rely on the monsoon. The rains arrived in May or June, filled the rice fields, and stopped by November. Today, however, the seasons have become increasingly unpredictable. Some years bring long periods of drought, when rivers dry up and crops fail; others bring torrential rain that destroys homes and washes away the soil.
Scientists link these changes to the global climate crisis, driven largely by carbon emissions from factories, power stations and cars. But local factors make the situation worse. Deforestation in the north has removed many of the trees whose roots once held the soil in place, increasing erosion and the risk of landslides. Air pollution from burning crops adds to the problem every dry season.
The damage is not only to people. As forests shrink, many animals lose their habitat, and some species are now close to becoming extinct. Because every part of an ecosystem depends on the others, the loss of a single species can have unexpected effects, from fewer bees to pollinate crops to more insects that damage them. Even the gentle drizzle that once fell for days in the cool season seems to have become rare. Experts agree that protecting forests is one of the cheapest and most effective ways to adapt to a warmer world, alongside cutting emissions.

q.fix: If it doesn't rain tomorrow, we will go for a picnic.
q.en: In the if-part of a first conditional we use Present Simple, not 'will': doesn't rain.

x: 'will' is correct in the result part.

is ถูกต้อง

is being cut down เป็น passive ถูกต้อง

q.s: When do storms often happen in the rainy season?
q.en: 'There is often a big storm in the afternoon.'
q.th: มักมีพายุใหญ่ในตอนบ่าย
x: Morning fog is mentioned for the cool season.
หมอกตอนเช้าพูดถึงในฤดูหนาว
Night is mentioned for cold in the north.
กลางคืนพูดถึงความหนาวในภาคเหนือ
Storms are 'often' in the rainy season.
มีพายุบ่อยในฤดูฝน

q.s: Why do some people travel to the north in the cool season?
o: To see the forest and the morning fog
q.en: 'Some people travel there to see the forest and the fog in the morning.'
q.th: บางคนไปภาคเหนือเพื่อดูป่าและหมอกตอนเช้า
x: 'It never snows in Thailand!'
ประเทศไทยหิมะไม่ตก
Beaches and islands are in the south.
ชายหาดและเกาะอยู่ทางใต้
Islands are in the south.
เกาะอยู่ทางใต้

q.s: Which sentence is TRUE?
o: The cool season is the worst time for tourists.
It is always cold in the south.
The hot season is usually cloudy.
q.en: The last sentence: 'It never snows in Thailand!'
q.th: ประโยคสุดท้ายบอกว่าประเทศไทยหิมะไม่ตกเลย
x: It's 'the best time for tourists'.
เป็นช่วงที่ดีที่สุดสำหรับนักท่องเที่ยว
Cold is mentioned in the north, at night.
ความหนาวพูดถึงภาคเหนือตอนกลางคืน
The hot season is 'clear and sunny'.
ฤดูร้อนท้องฟ้าแจ่มใสและมีแดด

q.s: Why were many people happy to hear about the storm?
o: They had had very hot weather for two weeks.
q.en: After a two-week heatwave, people were 'relieved' that a storm was coming.
q.th: หลังจากร้อนจัดสองสัปดาห์ ผู้คนจึงโล่งใจที่พายุจะมา
x: Not stated.
ไม่ได้บอก
Not stated.
ไม่ได้บอก
Not stated.
ไม่ได้บอก

q.s: What happened first when the storm started?
q.en: 'At around nine… the wind suddenly became stronger. Then the lightning started…'
q.th: ประมาณสามทุ่มลมแรงขึ้นก่อน แล้วจึงมีฟ้าแลบ
x: Flooding came after two hours of rain.
น้ำท่วมเกิดหลังฝนตกหนัก
Fallen trees were seen the next morning.
เห็นต้นไม้ล้มในเช้าวันถัดมา
Alarms went off after the lightning and thunder.
สัญญาณกันขโมยดังหลังฟ้าแลบและฟ้าร้อง

q.s: Why did car alarms go off?
q.en: '…thunder so loud that car alarms went off.'
q.th: ฟ้าร้องดังมากจนสัญญาณกันขโมยรถดัง
x: Not stated.
ไม่ได้บอก
Not stated as the reason.
ไม่ได้เป็นเหตุผลที่บอก
Not stated.
ไม่ได้บอก

q.s: What was the weather like the next morning?
q.en: 'The air felt fresh and almost cool, though nobody would call it freezing.'
q.th: อากาศสดชื่นและค่อนข้างเย็น แต่ไม่ถึงกับหนาวจัด
x: 'Nobody would call it freezing.'
ไม่มีใครเรียกว่าหนาวจัด
That was before the storm.
นั่นคือก่อนพายุ
The storm was the night before.
พายุเกิดเมื่อคืนก่อน

q.s: How does the shopkeeper feel?
o: He doesn't like floods but is glad the heat ended.
He is very angry about the storm.
q.en: 'I hate floods, but after two weeks of that heat, I'm not complaining.'
q.th: เขาเกลียดน้ำท่วม แต่หลังจากร้อนมาสองสัปดาห์ เขาก็ไม่บ่น
x: He says 'I hate floods'.
เขาบอกว่าเกลียดน้ำท่วม
He says 'I'm not complaining'.
เขาบอกว่าไม่บ่น
He was glad the heat ended.
เขาดีใจที่ความร้อนหมดไป

q.s: What has changed about the monsoon?
o: It has become harder to predict.
It no longer brings any rain.
q.en: 'Today, however, the seasons have become increasingly unpredictable.'
q.th: ปัจจุบันฤดูกาลคาดเดาได้ยากขึ้นเรื่อยๆ
x: November is when the rains used to stop.
พฤศจิกายนคือช่วงที่ฝนเคยหยุด
Some years bring torrential rain.
บางปีฝนตกหนักมาก
Not stated.
ไม่ได้บอก

q.s: According to the passage, why has erosion increased in the north?
o: Trees whose roots held the soil have been cut down.
q.en: 'Deforestation… has removed many of the trees whose roots once held the soil in place, increasing erosion.'
q.th: การตัดไม้ทำลายรากที่เคยยึดดินไว้ ทำให้การกัดเซาะเพิ่มขึ้น
x: Drought is a separate problem.
ภัยแล้งเป็นปัญหาแยกต่างหาก
Burning crops causes air pollution.
การเผาทำให้เกิดมลพิษทางอากาศ
Habitat loss is a result, not a cause, of erosion.
การสูญเสียถิ่นที่อยู่เป็นผลกระทบ ไม่ใช่สาเหตุของการกัดเซาะ

q.s: Which sources of carbon emissions are mentioned?
q.en: 'Carbon emissions from factories, power stations and cars.'
q.th: การปล่อยคาร์บอนจากโรงงาน โรงไฟฟ้า และรถยนต์
x: Not mentioned as emission sources.
ไม่ได้พูดถึงว่าเป็นแหล่งปล่อยคาร์บอน
Not mentioned.
ไม่ได้กล่าวถึง
Landslides are a result, not a source.
ดินถล่มเป็นผลกระทบ

q.s: Why can the loss of one species have 'unexpected effects'?
o: Every part of an ecosystem depends on the others.
q.en: 'Because every part of an ecosystem depends on the others…'
q.th: เพราะทุกส่วนของระบบนิเวศพึ่งพาอาศัยกัน
x: The passage mentions 'fewer bees', not extinct bees.
บทความบอกว่าผึ้งน้อยลง ไม่ใช่สูญพันธุ์
Not stated.
ไม่ได้บอก
Forests are shrinking.
ป่ากำลังลดลง

q.s: What do experts agree on?
o: Protecting forests is a cheap and effective way to adapt.
The monsoon will soon return to normal.
q.en: 'Experts agree that protecting forests is one of the cheapest and most effective ways to adapt.'
q.th: ผู้เชี่ยวชาญเห็นตรงกันว่าการปกป้องป่าเป็นวิธีที่ถูกและได้ผลที่สุดวิธีหนึ่ง
x: They recommend cutting emissions too.
พวกเขาแนะนำให้ลดการปล่อยก๊าซด้วย
Not stated.
ไม่ได้บอก
Not stated.
ไม่ได้บอก
